CMO Dashboard / Search Optimization
Workstream · Search Optimization Enterprise

Organic visibility, everywhere it's earned — search engines and AI answer engines alike.

SEO, AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), and GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) in one continuously-monitored workstream: site health, keyword and FAQ opportunities, a content audit, AI-answer-engine citation tracking, and standard GA4 reporting.

🛠 Site Health & Technical SEO

Crawl findings that affect whether search engines can properly reach, render, and rank this site — broken links and redirect chains, missing metadata, Core Web Vitals, robots/sitemap issues. Last crawled .

Structured Data / Schema Coverage

Whether the pages that most need it carry valid schema markup — the on-ramp to both classic rich results and AI-answer-engine citation eligibility.

Redirects & 404 Monitor

Broken and chained redirects, caught proactively rather than only after a crawl finds the dead link downstream.

🔑 Keyword & FAQ Opportunities

External opportunities that support organic performance — keyword gaps against the account's real ranking position, plus FAQ questions worth targeting because no existing content answers them yet.

FAQ ideas to think about
Rank Tracking

Position history for the keywords above, not just a single snapshot — a quick-win candidate is only a quick win if it's actually moving.

AI-Drafted Content Briefs

A ready hand-off from a keyword opportunity straight into Content Development — target entities, the questions competitor content leaves unanswered, and the specific gap to win on.

📰 Content Audit

Published content — including press releases — checked for whether it's still earning its keep: indexed and ranking, quietly going stale, or actively losing ground to competitor content.

Content Gap Analysis

Topics named competitors rank for that this account doesn't have content for at all.

Cannibalization Detector

Pages on this site competing against each other for the same query, splitting authority that should be consolidated behind one.

🤖 AEO / GEO Visibility

Whether this brand is actually being cited when people ask AI answer engines the questions it should be showing up for — the newest layer of "search," running alongside classic SEO rather than replacing it.

AI Citation Share of Voice

How often this brand is cited versus named competitors across the same monitored engine set — not just a yes/no per engine.

Backlink & Authority Monitor

New and lost referring domains, with toxic links flagged — the link-graph signal search engines (and, increasingly, AI answer engines) still weigh heavily.

📊 GA4 Standard Reports

Organic performance read directly from this account's GA4 property — sessions, conversions, and the landing pages actually earning organic traffic.

Anomaly Alerts

A sudden move flagged with a likely cause attached — cross-referenced against this workstream's own technical findings rather than left as a bare number.

🤝 Specialty Partners

Vetted partners that go deeper than this workstream builds in-house — activate an existing license or request a new relationship, and Verilume handles the vetting and, where a referral applies, earns a referral fee for the introduction.

    ✦
    US zip codes only — a non-US postal code (letters in the code, e.g. Canadian or European formats) is rejected outright rather than silently coerced into a real US zip that doesn't match the actual address, and every rejection stays on this upload's audit trail. Count-weighted by default; upload a revenue/order-value column and every zip has to have one before this will offer revenue-weighting instead — a partial revenue file stays count-weighted rather than quietly averaging over the gaps. The composite score/opportunity tier blend (two-thirds volume, one-third index by default) and the Holdout group size (about a sixth of scoreable zips by default) are both open, adjustable assumptions, not settled facts — flagged as such in the results below. This is zip-level only for now (DMA rollup needs a licensed Nielsen crosswalk or the FCC's public approximation, neither loaded in this build yet), and match-market pairing is based on who lives in a zip today, not real campaign performance history or geographic media-market adjacency — treat it as a starting shortlist for your own judgment, not a finished test plan.

    Upload your customer file

    📤

    Accepts .csv or .xlsx. Needs at minimum a zip code column — one row per transaction is the normal case (each row counts as one), or map a Customer Count column if the file already arrives pre-aggregated by zip. A revenue/order-value column is optional and unlocks revenue-weighting once every zip has one. Any extra columns are fine, just leave them mapped to "Ignore" below.

      CMO Dashboard / Media Plan
      Media Plan

      Annual Media Plan

      Built from what the brand needs on an ongoing basis — not a response to any one campaign. Allocates the annual budget across the Media Loop stages, then across channels within each stage, with a recommended starting split you can adjust anywhere. Campaigns can draw against these allocations, or run Unplanned, outside the plan entirely — see cxmedia-media-plan-budget-scope.md for the full design.

      Budget upload

      Upload your annual marketing budget in whatever format it's already in — the platform tries to auto-recognize a standard layout (Category, Working/Non-Working, Jan–Dec, Total) and tells you plainly what it found: a clean match, or specific columns/rows that need you to confirm before anything is saved.

      ✦
      This looks for month names (Jan–Dec) across every row to find your file's header(s) — if it finds exactly one, that's a standard flat table. If it finds several (a client export that repeats a header block per category, like a real Print/Direct Mail/Digital/Trade section layout), that's reported as a multi-block file: month and total columns still auto-recognize from their own header text, but the category-name and Working/Non-Working columns usually aren't labeled clearly enough to guess, so you confirm those. It also checks the math — if one row's total equals the sum of the others in its block, that's very likely a subtotal, not its own line item, and gets flagged so it isn't double-counted (or silently dropped).
